newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian spot gas slightly higher, weakness seen.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot gas slightly higher, weakness seen.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were slightly higher on Wednesday but traders said they expected values to decline before the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.

Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was discussed at C$1.46/1.47 per gigajoule, up from C$1.45/1.465 per GJ on Tuesday but down from June spot prices of C$1.57/1.62 last Wednesday. August AECO fetched C$1.44/1.47, marketers said.
Storage injections in Alberta totalled a hefty 1.4 billion cubic feet per day on Tuesday, despite lower field receipts, a Calgary-based trader said.

"Injections are going in twice as hard as normal," the trader said, adding that injections averaging about 700 million cubic feet a day were needed to get gas in storage to 90 percent of capacity by the end of October.

Prices in Alberta and British Columbia were expected to fall from Wednesday's levels later in the week with the approach of the U.S. holiday, traditionally the weakest time of the year for export demand, marketers said.
Eastern North American demand was already said to be weakening, with volumes through Empress on the Alberta-Saskatchewan border well below capacity.
The lower demand has resulted in a AECO-Empress transport charge of 1-2 cents for day gas, down from the usual 10 cents.
In British Columbia, day prices were also slightly higher on Wednesday. Sumas, Washington gas was talked at US$1.15 per million British Thermal units, up about 5 cents from Tuesday's lows.
"Short-term, prices will come off but on Monday they should come back," a trader of B.C. gas said.

In the east, cash prices at Dawn and Niagara were quoted between US$2.26 and US$2.30 per mmBtu, down about 5 cents on the day. The August Dawn basis price was pegged at US$2.165. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
